task: Semantic Execution Intelligence: authorize explicit PO-governed planned route deletion before code while preserving Git D as mandatory completion proof.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: PR #666 current-main plan-only replay proves a phase-semantics gap: Plan Before Code can resolve a PO-forbidden legacy route only after Git D already exists, so it cannot authorize the deletion before implementation. Authorization and completion evidence are conflated. Planned projection must be able to model an explicit PO-governed planned deletion, while actual-diff/Edit-Time/Truth must still require real Git deletion and must not accept mere plan intent as completion.
observableOutcomes: Plan Before Code can authorize an explicitly declared planned deletion when the exact static route is forbidden by an active Product Owner instruction and the file is inside the planned transaction.
Planned deletion authority is represented separately from Git tombstone evidence and never appears as a completed tombstone.
Actual-diff architecture resolution does not use planned intent as completion evidence; until Git D exists the live forbidden route remains subject to normal fail-closed enforcement.
Unrelated, non-forbidden, dynamic/wildcard, or undeclared paths cannot gain planned-deletion authorization.
unresolvedRisks: Treating planned intent as completed deletion would create a false PASS.
A generic planned-deletion list could become an architecture bypass unless intersected with active PO forbidden static-route authority.
Using planned deletion authority during actual-diff validation could hide an implementation that never removed the forbidden route.

in: Existing Plan Before Code planned-projection semantics.
Existing Semantic Execution Route / Atlas architecture resolution for PO-governed static forbidden routes.
Regression coverage distinguishing planned authorization from Git-proven tombstone completion.
out: New gate, registry, exception system, or canonical domain ownership for the forbidden legacy route.
Weakening Edit-Time, PO instruction enforcement, Truth Gate, or Git D completion proof.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is a critical phase-boundary defect in a fail-closed pre-execution gate. The highest practical fix is an explicit planned-deletion state derived from the existing plan plus active PO instruction, kept semantically distinct from Git tombstone proof and adversarially tested against false completion and unrelated deletions.

acceptanceCriteria: A declared planned deletion of src/app/szallitas-es-fizetes/page.tsx is authorized in planned projection only when PO-INSTRUCTION-SHIPPING-PAYMENT-SEPARATE is active and forbids /szallitas-es-fizetes.
Planned authorization exposes distinct provenance/state and does not populate Git tombstone evidence.
The same path in actual-diff mode without Git D is not considered a completed instruction-governed tombstone.
An unrelated planned deletion or a dynamic/wildcard forbidden route remains unresolved.
When Git D exists, the existing tombstone path and completion semantics remain unchanged.
invariants: Planned intent is authorization, never completion evidence.
Git D remains mandatory for tombstone completion.
Only exact active forbidden static routes may be planned-deletion-authorized.
The planned path must be declared in the current plan transaction.
No canonical domain ownership is added to the forbidden legacy route.

failureModes: Plan-only work deadlocks because deletion proof is required before implementation authorization.
Planned deletion is mistakenly treated as completed tombstone.
An unrelated path gains deletion authorization from a broad matcher.
Actual implementation keeps the forbidden route but passes because the plan promised deletion.
edgeCases: Plan-only projection with active exact forbidden static route.
Same plan after implementation with real Git D.
Declared planned deletion unrelated to any PO instruction.
File declared for deletion but still live during actual-diff validation.

alternatives.summary: Add explicit planned-deletion authorization to planned projection while preserving Git tombstone proof for actual completion.
alternatives.reason: Separates authorization from evidence without weakening fail-closed completion semantics.

alternatives.summary: Keep current behavior and require deletion before Plan Before Code can pass.
alternatives.reason: Violates plan-before-code ordering and makes valid deletion work impossible to authorize pre-execution.

alternatives.summary: Treat any path named in the plan as architecture-resolved.
alternatives.reason: Would turn plan metadata into a broad architecture bypass.

specialistReviews.finding: Authorization state and completion state must be distinct.
specialistReviews.resolution: Introduce planned-deletion provenance/state only for planned projection; retain Git tombstone semantics unchanged.

specialistReviews.finding: A plan declaration alone is self-asserted and cannot prove deletion.
specialistReviews.resolution: Intersect planned declaration with active PO forbidden static-route authority, and never expose it as Git tombstone evidence.

specialistReviews.finding: The fix must not reopen generic deleted-file architecture bypasses.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add negative controls for unrelated/deactivated/dynamic planned deletions and preserve existing tombstone tests.

specialistReviews.finding: Actual diff must not inherit planned-only authorization after edits begin.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use phase-specific architecture resolution: planned authorization for projected scope, Git-evidence-only resolution for actual scope.

challenge.scenario: Plan-only #666 declares removal of /szallitas-es-fizetes before any Git D exists.
challenge.finding: Current Plan Gate deadlocks on ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED.
challenge.resolution: Allow exact PO-governed planned deletion in planned projection.

challenge.scenario: The same route is still live after unrelated implementation edits.
challenge.finding: Plan intent must not count as completed removal.
challenge.resolution: Actual-diff architecture uses Git tombstones only; planned authorization is projection-only.

challenge.scenario: A developer declares deletion of an unrelated unowned route.
challenge.finding: Plan metadata could become a bypass.
challenge.resolution: Require exact intersection with an active forbidden static route from durable PO authority.

challenge.finding: Historical intent must not authorize new deletion work.

challenge.scenario: Forbidden state is dynamic or wildcard route.
challenge.finding: It cannot map safely to one filesystem page.

challenge.scenario: Planned path is not inside plannedFilePatterns / semantic mustEdit.
challenge.finding: Out-of-transaction deletion could be silently authorized.
challenge.resolution: Require planned declaration to be inside the current plan envelope and generated execution route.

challenge.scenario: Git D later appears for the exact route.
challenge.finding: Planned state must converge to existing tombstone semantics without a second authority model.
challenge.resolution: Git tombstone remains canonical completion evidence and supersedes planned-only state.

challenge.scenario: Plan declares deletion but implementation instead edits the route and keeps it alive.
challenge.finding: A false completion PASS would be catastrophic.
challenge.resolution: Edit-Time PO forbidden-state enforcement and actual architecture resolution remain live-state/Git-evidence based; planned intent cannot satisfy them.

proofPlan: Run plan-only Plan Before Code on this Control Plane change before implementation.
Unit-test planned PO-governed static deletion authorization with no Git D and assert distinct planned state.
Negative-control unrelated, inactive, dynamic and actual-diff-without-Git-D cases.
Preserve existing Git-proven tombstone tests and require them to remain PASS.
Run exact-head Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Quality, TypeScript, Production Build and Completion Truth; CLOSE→LEARN before merge.
After merge replay PR #666 plan-only unchanged in product intent and require Plan Before Code PASS before storefront implementation replay.

requirements.requirement: Plan Before Code authorizes only exact active-PO-governed planned static route deletion without representing it as completed Git tombstone evidence.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Planned intent may not be reported as Git-proven deletion or satisfy actual-diff completion.
Unrelated/inactive/dynamic planned deletions must remain unresolved.

requirements.requirement: The phase-aware Semantic Execution/Plan Gate change passes exact-head typecheck and production build.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The correction must not introduce type or production build regressions.

notes: Targeted follow-up discovered by #666 plan-only replay after merged #675 and #677. The defect is phase semantics, not storefront scope: planning authorization currently requires completion evidence. No product code or generic architecture exception in this transaction.
